verdict.summary: You need a bexio account. Then you log in to developer.bexio.com, accept the terms, create an app with a redirect URL and copy the client ID and secret. bexio says it does not restrict API access, and the findings show no review step for a plain OAuth app. Review only applies if you want a listing on the bexio marketplace, which is optional and requires existing customers and a revenue-share agreement.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus weeks to months of business work if you want a marketplace listing)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min after you have a bexio account
verdict.approval_wait: none for OAuth use (marketplace listing: no timeline published)

gates.name: Developer portal app
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own bexio company through your own client ID and secret.
limits: You need a bexio account (a trial works) and must accept the developer portal terms
Redirect URLs must be registered on the app and must match exactly
API calls use your own bexio user rights as well as the granted scopes
Per-company rate limit per minute. The number isn't published; read the RateLimit-* headers

gates.name: Other bexio users (no separate test mode documented)
gates.unlocks: Any other bexio user or company can authorize the same app. No test-user allowlist or development mode was found.
limits: No documented user cap or install cap for unlisted apps (not confirmed)
Each connection only has the bexio user rights of the person who authorized it
Refresh tokens require offline_access. The offline session closes after 1 year without renewal

gates.name: Public use (marketplace listing optional)
gates.unlocks: Anyone can connect without review, because bexio does not restrict API access. A listing on the bexio marketplace is a separate partner track that needs an application and a signed partner agreement.
limits: Marketplace requirements: at least 10 bexio customers, at least 20 active users, bexio API and OpenID Connect login, app in 2 of 4 languages (DE/FR/IT/EN), listing content in all 4
Marketplace terms: 25% service fee on revenue from shared bexio users (20% for top-revenue partners), bexio collects payments, price parity, you support your own customers
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for public OAuth use. Marketplace: no timeline published

steps.title: Get a bexio account
steps.detail: Sign up for a bexio account (a trial works) at bexio.com. You will use these credentials to log in to the developer portal.
gotchas: Third-party guides say you need an admin account to create apps. bexio's own docs don't say this.

steps.title: Log in to the bexio Developer Portal
steps.detail: Go to https://developer.bexio.com and log in with your bexio credentials.

steps.title: Accept the developer terms
steps.detail: Read and accept the portal terms and conditions. Pay attention to the commercial use rules in Section 4.4 before you build a paid product.
gotchas: Section 4.4 covers commercial use. Check it if you plan to charge for your integration.

steps.title: Create the app and set the redirect URL
steps.detail: Create a new app in the portal. In the 'Allowed redirect URL' field, enter the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. bexio requires redirect URLs when you register the app, and they must match exactly.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The Composio catalog lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add as the default, but a probe used https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Copy the URL from your auth config, and consider registering both. A third-party guide says an app can have up to 10 redirect URLs.
If the URL doesn't match exactly, sign-in stops with an error.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Open 'App Details' for the new app and reveal the Client ID and Client Secret. Store the secret on the server side only, because bexio requires it for the code exchange.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope list
steps.detail: Trim Composio's default list of about 37 scopes down to what your agent actually uses. Scopes are separated by spaces, and a write scope also grants read on the same resource. Include openid and offline_access so you get a refresh token.
gotchas: Scopes are fixed once the user consents. Adding scopes later means every user has to authorize again.
Payroll scopes give access to employee and paystub data. Leave them out unless you need them.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a bexio auth config that uses your own OAuth app. Composio has no managed app for bexio. Enter the Client ID, Client Secret and your trimmed scopes. The endpoints are https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth and .../token. The issuer is https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio.
gotchas: Use the realm-specific discovery path. The generic auth.bexio.com/.well-known path returns 404.
The token endpoint only accepts parameters in the request body, not in the query string.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, sign in to bexio, approve the consent screen and make a simple API call, for example listing contacts. If you see 'Client nicht gefunden', the client ID is wrong.
gotchas: Calls can still fail if your bexio user doesn't have rights to that data, even when the scope is granted.

steps.title: Roll out to other bexio users and handle rate limits
steps.detail: Other bexio companies can connect through the same app without review. Read RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset from responses and back off on HTTP 429, because the numeric limit isn't published.

steps.title: (Optional) Apply for a bexio marketplace listing
steps.detail: Only do this if you want to be listed on the bexio marketplace. You need at least 10 bexio customers and 20 active users, OpenID Connect login, the app in 2 of 4 languages and listing texts and visuals in all 4. Then submit the partner form and sign the partner agreement (25% revenue fee, bexio collects payments).

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for the partnership process
steps.detail: After you submit the form, bexio runs a partnership process. No timeline or review criteria beyond the listed requirements are published.

requirements.detail: Needed to log in to developer.bexio.com. A trial account works.

requirements.item: Accept the developer portal terms (Section 4.4 commercial use)
requirements.detail: You must accept them before you can create an app.
Must be set when you create the app and must match the callback exactly.
The authorization code flow requires the client secret at the token exchange. PKCE is not documented.

requirements.item: Marketplace: 10+ bexio customers and 20+ active users
requirements.detail: Only needed for a marketplace listing, not for public OAuth use.
App in 2 of DE/FR/IT/EN, listing content in all 4, and you support your own customers.
25% service fee (20% for top partners), bexio collects payments, price parity.

scopes.effect: OpenID Connect sign-in. Required for the OIDC flow.
Needed to get a refresh token. The offline session closes after 1 year without renewal.
Write access. Read access on the same resource is granted automatically. No review is tied to any scope.
Read and write access to the inbox.
Part of Composio's default list. bexio doesn't classify them as sensitive, but leave them out unless you need them, because adding scopes later means every user has to authorize again.

blockers.symptom: Login page shows 'Something went wrong. Client nicht gefunden.' (HTTP 400)
blockers.cause: The client_id is wrong or unknown to bexio.
blockers.fix: Copy the Client ID again from 'App Details' in the developer portal into your Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Sign-in stops with a redirect error
blockers.cause: The redirect URI Composio sends doesn't exactly match an 'Allowed redirect URL' on the app.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the app's allowed redirect URLs.

blockers.cause: Per-company per-minute rate limit. The number isn't published.
blockers.fix: Read the RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset headers and back off.

blockers.symptom: Calls are denied after you add new features
blockers.cause: Scopes are fixed at consent, and refreshing the token doesn't add scopes. Calls are also limited by the user's own bexio rights.
blockers.fix: Have users authorize again with the new scope list, and check the bexio user rights of whoever authorized.

blockers.cause: Parameters were sent in the query string.
blockers.fix: Send all token endpoint parameters in the POST body.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio, so you must register your own app in developer.bexio.com and enter its Client ID and Secret in a Composio auth config. This is quick and needs no review. Register the exact callback URL shown in your auth config as an 'Allowed redirect URL'. The catalog default is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but a probe used .../api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Trim the default scope list of about 37 scopes to what you need, because changing scopes later means every user has to authorize again.

evidence.quote: Go to the developer portal at https://developer.bexio.com and log in using your bexio credentials.

evidence.claim: You must accept the portal terms before creating an app, with attention to Section 4.4 commercial use.
evidence.quote: Read and accept the terms and conditions (please pay special attention to the commercial use regulations mentioned in Section 4.4).

evidence.claim: bexio does not restrict API access; anyone can build an integration.
evidence.quote: We do not restrict API access: anyone can develop an integration with bexio.

evidence.claim: Create an app, define 'Allowed redirect URL', then reveal the Client ID and Secret under 'App Details'.

evidence.claim: Up to ten redirect addresses per app (third-party guide).

evidence.claim: The redirect URL must match the portal entry exactly.

evidence.claim: Authorization code flow with the client secret at exchange; the app must be server-side.

evidence.claim: The OIDC issuer is https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio.
evidence.quote: Issuer https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio

evidence.claim: The realm discovery document is published and returns the issuer.
evidence.quote: "issuer":"https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio"

evidence.claim: The generic discovery path returns 404.
An invalid client_id returns HTTP 400 'Client nicht gefunden'.

evidence.claim: A write scope automatically grants read access to the same resource.

evidence.claim: Scopes are separated by whitespace.

evidence.claim: New scopes require going through authorization again.

evidence.claim: API access is limited by both the granted scopes and the authorizing user's rights.
evidence.quote: The API access happens with the user rights of the user who set up the connection to the application.

evidence.claim: Refresh tokens come with offline_access; the offline session closes after 1 year without renewal.
evidence.quote: The returned refresh token will be valid indefinitely but the associated offline session will be closed if not renewed within 1 year.

evidence.claim: Refresh uses grant_type refresh_token.
evidence.quote: Make sure you use the grant type "refresh_token".

evidence.claim: Token endpoint parameters must be in the request body.
evidence.quote: all parameters must be passed in the request body.

open_questions: Which Composio callback URL (v1 auth-apps/add or v3 toolkits/auth/callback) your auth config uses, and whether bexio accepts it. Neither was tested.
Whether an unlisted developer-portal app has any install cap, user cap or development-mode restriction isn't documented.
Whether you need a bexio admin account to create apps. Third-party guides say yes, bexio's docs don't say.
Whether bexio supports PKCE isn't documented.
Access token lifetime isn't stated. Only the 1-year offline session idle timeout is documented.
No timeline is published for the marketplace partnership process.
What exactly Section 4.4 (commercial use) of the developer terms requires wasn't retrieved.
